transcript:
Header: 2026-10-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Li (Redwood SE), Janelle Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Rosa Martínez (Everett ML), Ethan Brooks (Infra), Liam Chen (Procurement), Priya Nair (Data Eng)

Summary: quick check-in ahead of Dec renewal; customer considering expansion to EU region and bigger committed units for next year, also asking about private/VPC options for EU data residency.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, happy to see you all. quick agenda — renewal timing, capacity needs for next year, and any open security questions.
00:12 Rosa: thanks maya, yeah we're sort of lining up things because our contract runs out mid-December, so we wanted to confirm options for adding eu region and locking in reserved capacity for summer peak.
00:22 Connor: cool; from an se side we'll want to baseline current p95/p99 and sample models. can you remind me which models and avg seq lengths you're running?
00:31 Rosa: mostly our forecasting ensembles, two transformer-ish models, seq lengths around 1k tokens sometimes, but a lot of short inferences as well; typical latency target is sub-200ms p95.
00:42 Ethan: and infra-wise we have lots of traffic during daylight hours in europe and, you know, during spring maintenance windows. we need predictable throughput — bursts are fine but we can't have major throttles.
00:54 Maya: totally. so there are two levers — reserved dedicated pools for predictable throughput and burst capacity for spikes. reserved reduces unit cost but you commit. we can model a 12-month extension with a tier that covers your baseline qps plus a small burst bucket.
01:10 Liam: procurement question — if we commit to 12 months, do we get price protection for added regions? also what about data residency and KMS for encryption at rest?
01:20 Janelle: yes we can include EU region pricing in the proposal; for keys we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations for private deployments and VPC. we'll include SOC2 docs and EU data flow notes.
01:34 Rosa: when you say private deployment do you mean fully on-prem or a private control plane in our VPC? our legal team prefers customer-managed keys and logs stored in region.
01:44 Connor: both options — Redwood Private can be deployed with a private control plane in your VPC, or on-prem packaging if needed. for EU-specific residency the VPC/private control plane usually satisfies audit. on-prem is available but is heavier.
01:56 Priya: quick note — our models reference some IP that can't leave EU jurisdiction for certain customers, so we need strong guarantees.
02:05 Maya: understood. we'll highlight data residency and KMS options in the quote. for performance: Connor, can you describe the benchmark plan?
02:13 Connor: yes, i'll spin up an eu test cluster (same instance types as our dedicated offering) and run a 48-hour sweep across their model set at their p95 target and peak qps. i'll capture latency, token throughput, and cost estimates. we'll also test with and without quantization/8-bit to show tradeoffs.
02:30 Rosa: that'd be great — also, could you test k-v cache behavior? our workloads have a lot of prefix reuse. if kv cache keeps warm we get much better tail latency.
02:40 Connor: absolutely, we'll include prefix/KV cache tests and simulated traffic patterns. note: cache warmup times may vary by model, we'll show that in the perf spreadsheet.
02:50 Ethan: in terms of networking, any extra egress fees for EU region when users are US-based? we need to model our cost.
02:59 Maya: we'll call out cross-region egress; for dedicated we can route by region to minimize egress, and we can suggest a routing policy so EU traffic stays in EU.
03:10 Liam: procurement timeline: if we have the quote by early Nov, legal can review and we can aim for sign-off mid-Dec. does that match your timeline?
03:18 Maya: yes, our suggested timeline is: quote this week, perf results next week, then finalize terms and get signatures in early/mid Dec.
03:25 Rosa: perfect. two risks to flag — one is latency spikes during maintenance windows, two is model memory usage causing OOMs on smaller instances. we've hit that before with other providers.
03:36 Connor: noted, for memory we can propose specific instance classes and quantization profiles — e.g., 16GB per-GPU vs 32GB depending on sequence lengths; we'll show cost delta. also we'll include fallback policies: if a model OOMs we can route to a compatible variant that is quantized.
03:53 Rosa: any limits on concurrent KV cache sizes or key eviction policies? we've seen eviction hurt p95.
04:00 Connor: eviction is LRU by default but we can tune cache sizes per-pool; on Dedicated you can allocate more memory for cache. we'll document recommended cache configs for your workload.
04:10 Priya: security question — do you provide audit logs with user-level access detail and tamper-proofing for compliance?
04:18 Janelle: yes we provide audit logs, and for private deployments logs can be pushed to your SIEM; tamper-proofing is via cloud KMS + retention controls. we'll attach SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
04:30 Ethan: for the EU region, are there pre-existing capacity reservations or will we need to provision new?
04:36 Maya: we'll provision new Dedicated pools for EU; if you commit we can reserve capacity to guarantee throughput. there's a lead time for GPU provisioning but we'll outline options — immediate burst via hosted capacity, or reserved for consistent baseline.
04:51 Rosa: one more - are there any competitors offering better latency in eu region for a similar price? we've been benchmarking a couple things.
04:58 Maya: generally folks compare us to Bedrock for broad coverage and Anthropic for some model choices. we win on the unified runtime + predictable SLOs and tooling (rollouts, tracing). we'll include a short competitive note in the proposal.
05:10 Liam: procurement flag — can you add standard termination clauses and an extension option (auto-renew with 30-day notice)?
05:19 Janelle: yes we can include an extension clause; we'll draft the standard terms and highlight the auto-renew options.
05:26 Connor: technical note — for EU deployment I'll need access to a subset of anonymized requests and a test model bundle; Rosa can share that to run accurate latencies.
05:36 Rosa: i'll get the sample model bundle and anonymized traces to you by Nov 3.
05:40 Maya: great. recap & next steps: we'll send a 12-month renewal + EU region quote with reserved capacity options and burst pricing (Maya), se to run EU perf tests and share spreadsheet (Connor), customer to share metrics and test bundle (Rosa), procurement to review terms (Liam).
05:58 Liam: sounds good. any final Qs?
06:02 Ethan: just one — if we later want on-prem, how disruptive is migration?
06:07 Connor: migration path exists; we'd coordinate a phased cutover, data plane continuity, and we'd run a canary to validate. more details in technical deep-dive.
06:16 Maya: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the quote and schedule the deep-dive.
06:20 Rosa: thank you both.

End of call.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings: 'k v cache' sometimes transcribed as 'kv cash', 'HSM' typed as 'h s m' etc. Links shared during call: /redwood/proposal/EVT-Q4 (internal), perf-spreadsheet link (to be shared).
